clue.text: Note pair including composer reversing in Parisian street

parts.note: B is a musical note

indicators.note: reversing tells us the whole assembly of note, pair and composer is read backwards
including means the pair holds the composer within it

parts.note: a pair is a duo
Maurice Ravel, the French composer

explanation.surface: Two musical notes and a composer somehow turn up in a Paris street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parisian street' points to the French word for a broad avenue; 'reversing' covers the whole assembly, not just the composer.
explanation.definitionFit: A boulevard is a broad tree-lined avenue, the typical street of Paris.

clue.text: I've Noah, strangely, as a literary hero

indicators.note: strangely signals that the letters of I've and Noah are put in an odd new order

explanation.surface: Someone claims an odd connection to Noah as a hero of literature.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of I'VE plus NOAH are rearranged; the apostrophe is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Walter Scott's novel is named after its knightly hero, Wilfred of the title.

clue.text: Sorting list for delivery of wedding flowers is my business

definitions.text: delivery of wedding flowers is my business

indicators.note: sorting means arranging, so the letters of list and for are put in a different order

explanation.surface: A tradesperson sorts a list for delivering wedding bouquets.
explanation.definitionFit: Supplying and delivering flowers for weddings is the trade of a shop selling blooms.

clue.text: One of millions all over Andes, primarily

definitions.text: One of millions all over Andes, primarily

indicators.note: over signals that the word all is turned round so it reads backwards

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for a million, so a single one of the millions

indicators.note: primarily picks out the first letter of Andes

explanation.surface: This South American animal is one of millions found across the Andes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all over' gives LLA, then M and the A that starts Andes; the whole clue also describes the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The domesticated camelid is found in huge numbers throughout the Andes mountains.

clue.text: Little-known Republican revolutionary repeatedly captures English

indicators.note: captures means the repeated pair takes the English letter inside it
repeatedly means the Republican and revolutionary pair appears twice in a row

parts.note: Che Guevara, the Argentine-born revolutionary

explanation.surface: An obscure Republican revolutionary keeps seizing English territory.
explanation.walkthrough: RCHE twice gives RCHERCHE, and E goes in after the first R.
explanation.definitionFit: The French loan word describes something rare, exotic and known only to the few, an obscure choice.

clue.text: What's concerning about one Internet message and clever reply

indicators.note: about means the word for concerning goes round the other pieces

parts.note: re means concerning or regarding
I is the Roman numeral for one
a post is a message put up online

explanation.surface: Someone asks what a single online message and a witty answer are about.
explanation.definitionFit: A riposte is a quick sharp retort, originally a fencing counter-thrust.

clue.text: Duty's hard in part of nuclear reactor

indicators.note: in means the letter for hard is placed inside the reactor part

parts.note: the core is the central part of a nuclear reactor where fission happens
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A difficult job in a nuclear power station's heart.
explanation.definitionFit: A chore is a routine task or duty, often a tedious one.

clue.text: Venom — a famous warplane made without wood

indicators.note: without means the wood is taken out of the warplane's name

parts.note: the Spitfire, the Second World War RAF fighter
fir is a softwood timber

explanation.surface: Spite is likened to a famous fighter plane built without timber.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spitfire was a British fighter plane in the Second World War; remove FIR from it.
explanation.definitionFit: Venom in the figurative sense is malice or bitter ill will.

clue.text: Where the Queen often sees racehorses tie

definitions.text: Where the Queen often sees racehorses

explanation.surface: The Queen often watches her horses race, wearing a tie.
explanation.walkthrough: Royal Ascot is a famous British horse-racing meeting the monarch attends each June.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascot is the Berkshire racecourse the monarch visits, and also a broad cravat-like neck scarf.

clue.text: Penetrate middle of America, although no Conservative

indicators.note: no means the Conservative letter is left out

parts.note: center is the American spelling of centre, meaning the middle

explanation.surface: Someone breaks into the heartland of America, though not as a Tory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle of America' means the word for middle as Americans spell it.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter is to go into or pierce, as to penetrate does.

clue.text: A person playing violin as a nipper

explanation.surface: A child playing the violin.
explanation.walkthrough: A nipper is British slang for a small child, which misleads; here it is a creature that nips, the fiddler crab.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiddler plays the fiddle, and the fiddler crab pinches with its outsized claw.

clue.text: One acting before the contract bid?

parts.note: pre is a prefix meaning before
a tender is a bid to win a contract

explanation.surface: Someone acts before making a bid for a contract.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretender is someone who acts or feigns, putting on a show.

clue.text: Energy displayed by second eleven, perhaps

parts.note: an eleven is a team, as in cricket or football

explanation.surface: The second eleven showed plenty of energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Steam means vigour or drive, as in running out of steam.

clue.text: Radioactive element — pure panic with lump all uncovered

indicators.note: all uncovered means each of the three words loses its outer letters

explanation.surface: Panic about a radioactive lump laid bare.
explanation.definitionFit: Element 92 is the radioactive metal used as nuclear fuel.

clue.text: Inside of larch, where bees lay down their honey store for the future

indicators.note: inside of means the inner letters of larch, dropping its first and last

parts.words: where bees lay down their honey
parts.note: bees store honey in a hive

explanation.surface: Inside a larch tree, bees lay down honey for the future.
explanation.definitionFit: An archive is a collection of records kept for posterity.

clue.text: Response about duet that's ruined, so it's said

indicators.note: about means the response goes round the other letters

parts.note: a reply is a response

indicators.note: ruined means the letters of duet are wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: A response to a ruined duet, according to rumour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's ruined' is the anagram signal, so the four letters of 'duet' are scrambled before going inside the response.
explanation.definitionFit: Reputedly means according to what people say or believe.

clue.text: What's needed to make end bend earlier

parts.words: What's needed to make end bend
parts.note: to turn the word end into bend, a letter B has to stand fore, or in front of, the E

explanation.surface: A riddle about how to make the end bend sooner.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the letters as B fore E: B placed in front of E turns 'end' into 'bend'.
explanation.definitionFit: Before used as an adverb means earlier or previously.

clue.text: Overrun by foreign troops after United Nations is idle

indicators.note: after means the word for overrun follows the United Nations abbreviation

parts.note: a country overrun by an enemy army is occupied

explanation.surface: A country overrun by invaders after UN action is left idle.
explanation.definitionFit: Unoccupied means not busy or doing nothing, as idle does.

clue.text: Turn over low bar in East End, thus finding material presented in court

indicators.note: turn over means the low bar's name is flipped to read backwards

parts.note: a dive is a seedy drinking place

indicators.note: Cockneys of London's East End famously drop their H sounds, so the H goes

parts.note: hence means thus or therefore

explanation.surface: Flipping a seedy East End bar yields something for a trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn over' makes EVID from DIVE; Cockney speech of London's East End drops initial H, so HENCE becomes ENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Evidence is the testimony and exhibits put before a court.

clue.text: Spies capturing gutted terrorist up in roof space

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the whole assembly reads from bottom to top
capturing means the spy agency holds the other letters

parts.note: the CIA is the American spy agency

indicators.note: gutted means the insides of terrorist are removed, leaving its outer letters

explanation.surface: Spies seize a disembowelled terrorist hiding in the loft.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' means reading upwards, turning the whole assembly; 'gutted' leaves only the outside letters of 'terrorist'.
explanation.definitionFit: An attic is the room or space just below a roof.

clue.text: Not the same if iron, right, is used to fill hollow

indicators.note: used to fill means the other pieces are put inside the hollow

parts.note: a dent is a hollow in a surface
taken as written
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: Things would be different if iron were used to fill the right hollow.
explanation.definitionFit: Different means unlike or distinct, so not the same.

clue.text: Hit barrier, needing operation

parts.note: a wall is a barrier

explanation.surface: Someone crashes into a wall and needs surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: A wallop is a heavy blow, and to wallop is to hit hard.

clue.text: Are hyena or cheetah regularly seeing this bird twice?

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the words or cheetah

explanation.surface: A question about seeing a bird among hyenas and cheetahs.
explanation.walkthrough: Every other letter of 'Are hyena' also gives the bird, which is why the clue says 'twice'.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhea is a large flightless South American bird like a small ostrich.

clue.text: Act ended unfortunately in decline

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests a mishap, so the letters of act ended are jumbled

explanation.surface: A performance came to an unhappy end in a declining theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Decadent describes a society or art in moral or cultural decay.

clue.text: Renewed vigour coming after one earlier turn

indicators.note: earlier means the first piece comes before the turn

parts.note: the second comes after the first, number one
to wind is to turn, as a handle

explanation.surface: Fresh energy arrives after an earlier turn.
explanation.definitionFit: A second wind is a fresh burst of energy after tiredness sets in.

clue.text: Get the better of more than political control

parts.note: over means more than, as in over fifty
power is political control, as in the party in power

explanation.surface: Winning more than political control lets you beat rivals.
explanation.definitionFit: To overpower is to overcome or defeat by greater strength.

clue.text: Flatter spades frequently weaken around middle of stock

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for spades in card games
oft is an old word for often

indicators.note: around means the word for weaken goes about the central letter

parts.note: to sap is to weaken or drain

indicators.note: middle of picks the central letter of stock

explanation.surface: Spades often weaken a garden's stock with flattery.
explanation.walkthrough: SAP goes around O, the middle letter of 'stock', to give SOAP.
explanation.definitionFit: To soft-soap someone is to persuade them with flattery.

clue.text: Tart cafe served up is a hand-made thing

indicators.note: served up suggests the letters of tart cafe are dished out in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A tart served at a cafe is a hand-made item.
explanation.definitionFit: An artefact is an object made by human hands, such as a tool or ornament.

clue.text: Far from firm identification, that's clear

parts.note: limp means floppy, far from firm

explanation.surface: A flimsy form of identification makes the matter clear.
explanation.definitionFit: Limpid means transparent or clear, as of water or prose.

clue.text: Irritable doctor unknown to consume alcoholic spirit

indicators.note: to consume means the doctor and the unknown take the spirit inside

parts.note: a GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor
rum is a spirit distilled from sugar cane
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A cranky doctor of unknown name drinks rum.
explanation.definitionFit: Grumpy means bad-tempered and irritable.

clue.text: Provide with stock European joke

parts.note: a quip is a witty joke

explanation.surface: Supplying stock to a European with a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: To equip is to furnish or supply with what is needed.

clue.text: Lacking time to educate every one

indicators.note: lacking means the letter for time is left out

parts.note: to teach is to educate

explanation.surface: With no time to educate every pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: Each means every one taken individually.
